source_locations.location: Abstract; reaction equation (1); crystal data in Notes and references

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete tetranuclear bowl contains seven bridging fluorides and four capping 15-crown-5 ligands. Its puckered Gd–F ring has two pairs of double fluoride bridges, two single bridges, and a transannular fluoride bridge between Gd(1) and Gd(3). Those two Gd centers are nine-coordinate; Gd(2) and Gd(4) are eight-coordinate. Five [AsF6]− counterions and six uncoordinated SO2 molecules occupy the lattice.

synthesis.procedure: Under dry nitrogen using dry-box and Schlenk techniques, GdF(AsF6)2 and 15-crown-5 were placed in a Lambda flask. Dry liquid SO2 was condensed separately into each arm at −30 °C. The solutions were mixed at 0 °C, warmed to room temperature, stirred for 1 h, and allowed to settle.
synthesis.temperature: SO2 condensed at −30 °C; solutions mixed at 0 °C, then warmed to room temperature; crystallized at −30 °C
synthesis.time: Stirred for 1 h; crystallized for one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Lambda flask; dry-box and Schlenk techniques under dry nitrogen
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After a brown gel-like precipitate settled, the supernatant was decanted and its liquid-SO2 volume reduced. Storage at −30 °C for one week afforded small colorless X-ray-quality crystals.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Vacuum drying removes lattice SO2 from the crystalline cluster salt, producing a powder that loses crystallinity. The article identifies the resulting SO2-free composition and reports IR and gadolinium-analysis evidence, but does not report a separate crystal structure for this powder.

synthesis.procedure: The reaction of GdF(AsF6)2 with 15-crown-5 in liquid SO2 was carried out under dry nitrogen as described for the crystalline solvate. After crystallization, the reaction mixture was dried under vacuum to give the SO2-free powder. An analogous reaction of [Gd(SO2)n(AsF6)3] with 15-crown-5 also gave a powder with a matching IR spectrum after vacuum drying.
